title: Global Diversity of Norovirus Genotypes from 2002 to 2025: A Review of Temporal, Age-Specific and Regional Trends
abstract: Norovirus is a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) worldwide, with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly in young children and older adults. This study characterizes the global prevalence and diversity of norovirus genotypes among sporadic cases. A review of English-language studies (published 2002–2026) that characterized norovirus genotype distribution among sporadic cases was conducted, excluding outbreak and asymptomatic detections. Pooled data were analyzed with stratifications by age group, region, and year of sample collection. A total of 20,588 cases were identified from 72 publications. There were 30 genotypes identified, with GII.4, GII.3, GII.2, GII.17, and GII.6 and each accounting for ≥5% of detections. GII.4 was the predominant genotype globally, accounting for 54% of cases and up to 80% among older adults across all years, but periodic fluctuation was seen, coinciding with fluctuations in the prevalence of other genotypes, especially GII.3, GII.2, and GII.17. Among GI genotypes, GI.3 was most prevalent (46%), particularly among adults. Genotype diversity was highest among children in low- and middle-income countries and in Asia/Oceania. Findings indicate that a small number of genotypes account for most cases. As genotyping characterizes the major capsid protein, the primary target of antibody recognition, findings have important implications for vaccine development and public health interventions.

title: Polyamine depletion inhibits murine and human norovirus infection
abstract: UNLABELLED: Noroviruses are non-enveloped, positive-sense RNA viruses in the family Caliciviridae. Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are the leading cause of viral gastrointestinal disease. Despite their clinical relevance, therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited, partly due to challenges in cultivating HNoV and limited understanding of virus-host interactions. Polyamines (PAs) are small polycationic metabolites derived from amino acid metabolism that are essential for diverse cellular functions and serve as important host factors for many RNA viruses. However, their role in norovirus infection has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate that PAs are critical for productive infection for both HNoV and murine norovirus (MNV), underscoring a conserved and functionally significant dependency across species. Functional analysis in MNV-infected cells showed that PA depletion resulted in a marked reduction in major capsid protein synthesis and reduced viral titers following the first replication cycle, coinciding with a loss of virus-induced cytopathic effect (CPE). In PA-depleted cells, viral titers and CPE could be restored by exogenous supplementation with spermine or spermidine (metabolites of the PA biosynthetic pathway), cholesterol, or a PI3-kinase inhibitor. In addition to MNV, depletion of PAs completely ablated HNoV infection in human intestinal enteroids, which was also partially rescued by adding exogenous PAs. Collectively, these findings identify PAs as a novel host dependency factor that facilitates norovirus infection and highlight PA metabolism as a potential therapeutic target for antiviral intervention against HNoV. IMPORTANCE: Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide, yet the development of effective antivirals and vaccines has been hampered by the lack of small-animal models and robust in vitro systems to propagate the virus. Murine norovirus (MNV) shares key features with HNoV and serves as a valuable surrogate for studying norovirus biology. In this study, we identify host-derived polyamines (PAs) as essential and conserved metabolites required for productive infection for both HNoV and MNV. PAs exert multifactorial effects on norovirus infection, particularly by facilitating virus-induced apoptosis and promoting virion release in MNV-infected cells. Notably, PA depletion using difluoromethylornithine (DFMO), a well-established inhibitor of PA synthesis, effectively suppressed MNV and HNoV infection. Therefore, our results provide new insights into norovirus-host interactions and highlight the potential of a host-targeting antiviral approach to limit norovirus infection. Furthermore, our findings provide a rationale for further investigating DFMO, a licensed and well-tolerated drug, as a potential therapeutic option for chronic norovirus infections in immunocompromised patients.

Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are the leading cause of viral gastrointestinal disease. Despite their clinical relevance, therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited, partly due to challenges in cultivating HNoV and limited understanding of virus-host interactions. Polyamines (PAs) are small polycationic metabolites derived from amino acid metabolism that are essential for diverse cellular functions and serve as important host factors for many RNA viruses. However, their role in norovirus infection has remained elusive. Here, we demonstrate that PAs are critical for productive infection for both HNoV and murine norovirus (MNV), underscoring a conserved and functionally significant dependency across species. Functional analysis in MNV-infected cells showed that PA depletion resulted in a marked reduction in major capsid protein synthesis and reduced viral titers following the first replication cycle, coinciding with a loss of virus-induced cytopathic effect (CPE). In PA-depleted cells, viral titers and CPE could be restored by exogenous supplementation with spermine or spermidine (metabolites of the PA biosynthetic pathway), cholesterol, or a PI3-kinase inhibitor. In addition to MNV, depletion of PAs completely ablated HNoV infection in human intestinal enteroids, which was also partially rescued by adding exogenous PAs. Collectively, these findings identify PAs as a novel host dependency factor that facilitates norovirus infection and highlight PA metabolism as a potential therapeutic target for antiviral intervention against HNoV. IMPORTANCE Human noroviruses (HNoVs) are a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide, yet the development of effective antivirals and vaccines has been hampered by the lack of small-animal models and robust in vitro systems to propagate the virus. Murine norovirus (MNV) shares key features with HNoV and serves as a valuable surrogate for studying norovirus biology. In this study, we identify host-derived polyamines (PAs) as essential and conserved metabolites required for productive infection for both HNoV and MNV. PAs exert multifactorial effects on norovirus infection, particularly by facilitating virus-induced apoptosis and promoting virion release in MNV-infected cells. Notably, PA depletion using difluoromethylornithine (DFMO), a well-established inhibitor of PA synthesis, effectively suppressed MNV and HNoV infection. Therefore, our results provide new insights into norovirus-host interactions and highlight the potential of a host-targeting antiviral approach to limit norovirus infection. Furthermore, our findings provide a rationale for further investigating DFMO, a licensed and well-tolerated drug, as a potential therapeutic option for chronic norovirus infections in immunocompromised patients.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of polyamines in norovirus infection, as therapeutic strategies for norovirus infections remain limited due to challenges in cultivating the virus and limited understanding of virus-host interactions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved both murine norovirus (MNV) and human norovirus (HNoV) using human intestinal enteroids as the host model. It was conducted in a laboratory setting with a focus on analyzing the effects of polyamine depletion on viral infection.
analysis.methods: The researchers used functional analysis in MNV-infected cells and human intestinal enteroids to assess the impact of polyamine depletion. They employed difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) to inhibit polyamine synthesis and evaluated viral titers, cytopathic effects, and protein synthesis.
analysis.main_results: Functional analysis showed that polyamine depletion significantly reduced major capsid protein synthesis and viral titers in MNV-infected cells. Similarly, HNoV infection was completely ablated in PA-depleted human intestinal enteroids.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings identify polyamines as a novel host dependency factor that facilitates norovirus infection and suggest that targeting PA metabolism could be a promising antiviral strategy for HNoV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide new insights into norovirus-host interactions and support the exploration of host-targeting antiviral approaches for limiting norovirus infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on laboratory models and does not include clinical trials. However, the evidence is strong as it directly demonstrates the role of polyamines in both MNV and HNoV infection using well-validated methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of polyamines in norovirus infection, highlighting their critical function in both murine norovirus (MNV) and human norovirus (HNoV). The research demonstrates that polyamine depletion significantly inhibits viral replication and cytopathic effects in MNV-infected cells and completely ablates HNoV infection in human intestinal enteroids. These findings identify polyamines as a novel host dependency factor for norovirus and suggest that targeting polyamine metabolism could offer new therapeutic strategies. The study uses laboratory models and well-established methods to validate its conclusions, providing strong evidence for the potential of host-targeting antiviral approaches. However, the results are based on in vitro systems and do not account for in vivo complexities, which limits their direct application to clinical settings.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究同时涉及小鼠诺如病毒(MNV)和人类诺如病毒(HNoV),使用人类肠道类器官作为宿主模型。研究在实验室环境中进行,重点分析多胺耗竭对病毒感染的影响。

abstract_zh: 未标注:诺如病毒是Caliciviridae科中的无包膜正链RNA病毒。人类诺如病毒(HNoVs)是病毒性胃肠疾病的主要病因。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但针对诺如病毒感染的治疗策略仍然有限,部分原因是HNoV培养的困难以及对病毒-宿主相互作用的理解不足。多胺(PAs)是源自氨基酸代谢的小分子多阳离子代谢物,对多种细胞功能至关重要,并且是许多RNA病毒的重要宿主因子。然而,其在诺如病毒感染中的作用仍不清楚。在这里,我们证明PAs对HNoV和小鼠诺如病毒(MNV)的有产感染至关重要,突显了跨物种的保守且功能重要的依赖性。在MNV感染的细胞中进行的功能分析显示,多胺耗竭导致主要衣壳蛋白合成显著减少,并在第一次复制周期后病毒滴度降低,这与病毒诱导的细胞病变效应(CPE)的丧失同时发生。在多胺耗竭的细胞中,通过外源性补充精胺或精脒(多胺生物合成途径的代谢物)、胆固醇或PI3-激酶抑制剂可以恢复病毒滴度和CPE。除了MNV之外,多胺耗竭完全消除了人类肠道类器官中的HNoV感染,这种效应在添加外源性多胺后部分恢复。这些发现识别出多胺作为新型宿主依赖因子,促进诺如病毒感染,并强调多胺代谢作为针对HNoV感染的潜在治疗靶点。重要性:人类诺如病毒(HNoVs)是全球急性病毒性胃肠炎的主要病因,但由于缺乏小型动物模型和有效的体外系统来传播病毒,开发有效的抗病毒药物和治疗手段受到了阻碍。小鼠诺如病毒(MNV)与HNoV共享关键特征,并可作为研究诺如病毒生物学的有价值的替代模型。在这项研究中,我们确定了源自宿主的多胺(PAs)作为HNoV和MNV有产感染所必需的保守代谢物。多胺对诺如病毒感染具有多方面的影响,特别是在促进病毒诱导的细胞凋亡和促进病毒颗粒释放方面。值得注意的是,使用多胺合成的已知抑制剂二氟甲基鸟氨酸(DFMO)进行多胺耗竭可有效抑制MNV和HNoV感染。因此,我们的结果为诺如病毒-宿主相互作用提供了新的见解,并突出了针对宿主的治疗策略在限制诺如病毒感染方面的潜力。此外,我们的发现为进一步研究DFMO,一种已获许可且耐受性良好的药物,作为免疫功能低下患者慢性诺如病毒感染的潜在治疗选项提供了依据。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨多胺在诺如病毒感染中的作用,因为针对诺如病毒感染的治疗策略仍然有限,这主要是由于病毒培养的困难以及对病毒-宿主相互作用的理解不足。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究同时涉及小鼠诺如病毒(MNV)和人类诺如病毒(HNoV),使用人类肠道类器官作为宿主模型。研究在实验室环境中进行,重点分析多胺耗竭对病毒感染的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员在MNV感染的细胞和人类肠道类器官中进行了功能分析,以评估多胺耗竭的影响。他们使用二氟甲基鸟氨酸(DFMO)来抑制多胺合成,并评估了病毒滴度、细胞病变效应和蛋白质合成。
analysis_zh.main_results: 功能分析显示,多胺耗竭显著降低了MNV感染细胞中的主要衣壳蛋白合成和病毒滴度。同样,在多胺耗竭的人类肠道类器官中,HNoV感染被完全消除。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现识别出多胺作为新型宿主依赖因子,促进诺如病毒感染,并建议针对多胺代谢的策略可能是HNoV感染的有前景的治疗手段。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为诺如病毒-宿主相互作用提供了新的见解,并支持探索针对宿主的治疗策略以限制诺如病毒感染,特别是在免疫功能低下患者中。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖于实验室模型,未包括临床试验。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它直接展示了多胺在MNV和HNoV感染中的作用,使用了经过验证的方法。

title: Human norovirus infection does not induce serotonin secretion in human intestinal organoids
abstract: ABSTRACT Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide. The primary symptoms of HuNoV-associated disease are vomiting and diarrhea; yet the mechanisms underlying these symptoms are poorly understood. Neuroactive hormones such as serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) secreted by intestinal enteroendocrine cells (EECs) can activate vomiting centers in the brain and play a critical role in regulating emetic signaling. Serotonin release from infected EECs has been implicated in vomiting during other enteric infections. Recent studies have reported the detection of HuNoV RNA and antigen in EECs in jejunal biopsies from immunocompromised patients with chronic HuNoV infection and rhesus macaques. We therefore investigated whether HuNoV infection of human intestinal organoids (HIOs) induces serotonin secretion. We examined infection and serotonin secretion with multiple genogroup II HuNoV strains using adult and infant jejunal HIO models, including a doxycycline-inducible neurogenin-3 HIO line with increased numbers of EECs. HuNoV infection did not induce serotonin secretion in either adult or infant HIOs as measured by ELISA. Consistent with enterocytes being the primary target cell type for HuNoVs, GII.4 HuNoV replication was robust in parental HIOs but reduced in EEC-enriched cultures. Furthermore, supernatants from parental HIOs failed to stimulate serotonin release from EEC-enriched HIOs. Together, these findings demonstrate that HuNoV infection of intestinal epithelial cells is insufficient to trigger serotonin release in HIOs. These results suggest that HuNoV-associated vomiting is unlikely to result from direct epithelial serotonin secretion and may require additional cellular components such as immune or neuronal signaling pathways or may involve other neuroactive hormones. IMPORTANCE Vomiting is a hallmark symptom of human norovirus disease. Yet, the biological mechanisms responsible for this response are unknown. Infection of enteroendocrine cells and secretion of serotonin play key roles in the emetic response to other gastrointestinal viruses such as rotavirus. Since recent studies have detected human norovirus antigens and RNA in enteroendocrine cells, we hypothesized that human norovirus infection could stimulate serotonin secretion. We used jejunal human intestinal organoids from adults and infants, including organoids enriched for enteroendocrine cells, and found that infection with several clinically important strains did not induce serotonin secretion, even under conditions supporting robust viral replication. These data indicate that serotonin release from intestinal epithelial cells alone is unlikely to explain norovirus-induced vomiting and highlights the need to investigate alternative mechanisms, including other neuroactive hormones, and neuronal signaling pathways to better understand the pathogenesis of norovirus-associated vomiting.

title_zh: 人类诺如病毒感染不会在人类肠道类器官中诱导血清素分泌
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide. The primary symptoms of HuNoV-associated disease are vomiting and diarrhea; yet the mechanisms underlying these symptoms are poorly understood. Neuroactive hormones such as serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine; 5-HT) secreted by intestinal enteroendocrine cells (EECs) can activate vomiting centers in the brain and play a critical role in regulating emetic signaling. Serotonin release from infected EECs has been implicated in vomiting during other enteric infections. Recent studies have reported the detection of HuNoV RNA and antigen in EECs in jejunal biopsies from immunocompromised patients with chronic HuNoV infection and rhesus macaques. We therefore investigated whether HuNoV infection of human intestinal organoids (HIOs) induces serotonin secretion. We examined infection and serotonin secretion with multiple genogroup II HuNoV strains using adult and infant jejunal HIO models, including a doxycycline-inducible neurogenin-3 HIO line with increased numbers of EECs. HuNoV infection did not induce serotonin secretion in either adult or infant HIOs as measured by ELISA. Consistent with enterocytes being the primary target cell type for HuNoVs, GII.4 HuNoV replication was robust in parental HIOs but reduced in EEC-enriched cultures. Furthermore, supernatants from parental HIOs failed to stimulate serotonin release from EEC-enriched HIOs. Together, these findings demonstrate that HuNoV infection of intestinal epithelial cells is insufficient to trigger serotonin release in HIOs. These results suggest that HuNoV-associated vomiting is unlikely to result from direct epithelial serotonin secretion and may require additional cellular components such as immune or neuronal signaling pathways or may involve other neuroactive hormones. IMPORTANCE Vomiting is a hallmark symptom of human norovirus disease. Yet, the biological mechanisms responsible for this response are unknown. Infection of enteroendocrine cells and secretion of serotonin play key roles in the emetic response to other gastrointestinal viruses such as rotavirus. Since recent studies have detected human norovirus antigens and RNA in enteroendocrine cells, we hypothesized that human norovirus infection could stimulate serotonin secretion. We used jejunal human intestinal organoids from adults and infants, including organoids enriched for enteroendocrine cells, and found that infection with several clinically important strains did not induce serotonin secretion, even under conditions supporting robust viral replication. These data indicate that serotonin release from intestinal epithelial cells alone is unlikely to explain norovirus-induced vomiting and highlights the need to investigate alternative mechanisms, including other neuroactive hormones, and neuronal signaling pathways to better understand the pathogenesis of norovirus-associated vomiting.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人类诺如病毒(HuNoVs)是全球急性胃肠炎的主要病因之一。HuNoV相关疾病的主要症状是呕吐和腹泻;然而,这些症状的发病机制仍不清楚。肠道内分泌细胞(EECs)分泌的神经活性激素如血清素(5-羟基色胺;5-HT)可以激活大脑中的呕吐中枢,并在调节呕吐信号中起关键作用。在其他肠道感染中,受感染的EECs释放血清素已被认为与呕吐有关。最近的研究报告称,在免疫功能低下且患有慢性HuNoV感染的患者以及恒河猴的空肠活检中检测到了HuNoV RNA和抗原。因此,我们研究了HuNoV感染是否会导致人类肠道类器官(HIOs)中的血清素分泌。我们使用成人和婴儿空肠HIO模型,包括一种四环素诱导的神经元生成素-3 HIO系,该系中EECs数量增加,来检测感染和血清素分泌情况。通过ELISA检测发现,无论是成人还是婴儿HIOs,HuNoV感染均未诱导血清素分泌。这与肠上皮细胞是HuNoV主要靶细胞类型一致,GII.4 HuNoV在亲本HIOs中复制旺盛,但在富含EECs的培养物中复制减少。此外,亲本HIOs的上清液未能刺激富含EECs的HIOs释放血清素。综上所述,这些发现表明HuNoV感染肠道上皮细胞不足以在HIOs中触发血清素释放。这些结果提示HuNoV相关的呕吐不太可能由直接的上皮血清素分泌引起,可能需要其他细胞成分,如免疫或神经信号通路,或者涉及其他神经活性激素。重要性 呕吐是人类诺如病毒疾病的一个标志性症状。然而,导致这种反应的生物学机制尚不清楚。在其他胃肠道病毒如轮状病毒的呕吐反应中,肠道内分泌细胞的感染和血清素的分泌起着关键作用。由于最近的研究在肠道内分泌细胞中检测到了人类诺如病毒抗原和RNA,我们假设人类诺如病毒感染可能刺激血清素分泌。我们使用了成人和婴儿的空肠类器官,包括富含肠道内分泌细胞的类器官,并发现几种临床重要的毒株感染并未诱导血清素分泌,即使在支持病毒高效复制的条件下也是如此。这些数据表明,仅由肠道上皮细胞释放血清素不足以解释诺如病毒引起的呕吐,强调了需要探索其他机制,包括其他神经活性激素和神经信号通路,以更好地理解诺如病毒相关呕吐的发病机制。

title: Prolonged Infectivity of Murine Norovirus in Aerosols Suggests Potential for Airborne Transmission.
abstract: Norovirus is a highly contagious enteric virus best known for fecal-oral transmission, but increasing evidence suggests that airborne spread may also contribute to outbreaks. Aerosol transmission of norovirus can occur during episodes involving vomiting, diarrhea, or toilet flushing. To investigate this possibility, the infectivity of aerosolized murine norovirus (MNV) was evaluated over time using influenza A virus (H1N1), a well-established respiratory virus transmitted via aerosols, as a reference control. Aerosols with a mass median aerodynamic diameter of 2.38 μm were generated in a 220 L chamber and captured using gelatin filters. MNV infectivity decreased by 2.33 log 10 within the first 3 hours but remained detectable for up to 9 hours, corresponding to a total reduction of 4.2 log 10 . In contrast, H1N1 exhibited a more rapid decay, with a 2.9 log 10 reduction within 3 hours. Overall, these results indicate that MNV retains airborne infectivity for longer durations, supporting the plausibility of aerosol transmission during norovirus outbreak scenarios.

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明气溶胶传播可能在诺如病毒 暴发中发挥作用,这可能对监测、诊断以及预防策略产生影响。这可能有助于改进预防诺如病毒传播的公共卫生措施。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括使用鼠源性诺如病毒作为模型,这可能无法完全代表人类诺如病毒。由于使用了替代病毒并需要进一步研究以在人类诺如病毒中确认这些发现,证据强度为中等。

title: Global resurgence of norovirus GII.17[P17] accompanies shifting phylogeographic connectivity patterns: surveillance in Jiangsu, 2023–2025
abstract: Background Norovirus GII.17[P17] has re-emerged and has been circulating globally since 2023. In Jiangsu, China, we found that its proportion increased from 2024 onward. Using local surveillance data combined with global sequences, we reconstructed the global spatiotemporal dynamics of GII.17[P17] and explored its evolution and molecular mechanisms. Methods Samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing using next-generation sequencing. We used bioinformatics tools to analyze the full viral protein 1 sequences for molecular evolution, spatiotemporal phylogeographic associations, and amino acid changes. Results From October 2024 to May 2025, 209 GII.17[P17] outbreaks were reported (approximately 26 per month), while only 23 outbreaks occurred in the full year of 2023 (fewer than 2 per month). In sporadic case surveillance, the proportion of GII.17[P17] increased from 9.6% in 2023 to 62.4% in January–May 2025. The maximum clade credibility tree showed that GII.17[P17] clustered into two large clusters. Most samples from 2024 to 2025 belonged to Lineage 3 of Cluster II. In the phylogenetic network and minimum spanning tree, we identified three core hub strains. Inferred phylogeographic connectivity patterns suggest a shift in the primary centers of viral lineage dispersal from East Asia (Cluster I, 2014–2016) to Northwest Europe (Cluster II, 2021–2025). Molecular evolutionary analysis revealed that the current dominant lineage (Lineage 3, Cluster II) exhibited an evolutionary rate of 4.126 × 10 −3 substitutions/site/year (95% HPD: 3.27–4.98 × 10 −3 ), substantially higher than the earlier Cluster I lineages (1.798 × 10 −3 ; 95% HPD: 1.41–2.19 × 10 −3 ; posterior probability >0.99; 95% HPD intervals non-overlapping). Conclusion Inferred phylogeographic connectivity patterns indicate that the primary centers of GII.17[P17] lineage dispersal have shifted from East Asia (2014–2016) to Northwest Europe (2021–2025). The current dominant lineage (Lineage 3, Cluster II) exhibits an accelerated evolutionary rate, approximately 2.3-fold faster than Cluster I lineages, and carries lineage-specific amino acid substitutions in antigenic epitopes temporally associated with its global expansion. These findings highlight the value of sustained genomic surveillance in regions with high inferred phylogeographic connectivity for monitoring norovirus evolution.

title: Evaluation of Human Norovirus Replication in Salivary Gland Cells
abstract: Abstract Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the most common cause of non-bacterial foodborne illnesses worldwide. HuNoVs are notoriously difficult to culture, and current cell culture systems, such as human intestinal enteroids have limitations in efficiency and scalability, which has limited their applications in food safety studies. Recently, it has been shown that transformed salivary gland cell lines (including NS-SV-TT-DC) allow for replication and passaging of norovirus GII.4. Herein, we examined whether we can independently observe viral replication in salivary gland cells and if other strains of human norovirus can replicate in these cells. For this purpose, we first evaluated the replication of several norovirus strains in NS-SV-TT-DC cells by either infecting them with vesicle-cloaked viruses or total viruses in stool filtrates. Low levels of viral replication was observed and vesicle isolation did not improve viral replication. Next, we screened for replication of 50 norovirus samples from 9 genotypes, and 14 isolates demonstrated over a two-fold viral replication. We observed that the initial viral load in the samples does not have a significant effect on replication efficiency. We were also able to successfully passage several isolates. Subsequently, we examined whether interferon inhibitors such as Ruxolitinib, TPCA-1, and BX795 would improve viral replication and observed negligible effects. Finally we tested multiple supplements including MgCl 2 , bile salt, ceramide, and TAK-779. Most supplements had little or no effect on HuNoV replication in NS-SV-TT-DC cells. Bile salt and TAK-779 showed limited, genotype-specific benefits. Altogether these results indicate that salivary gland cells allow limited replication of certain HuNoV isolates. Importance The lack of robust and accessible cell culture systems continues to hinder human norovirus research. Salivary gland cell lines have recently emerged as a promising alternative to human intestinal enteroids because they are easy to maintain and relatively unexpensive. Here, we provide a large-scale independent evaluation of the NS-SV-TT-DC salivary gland model using 50 clinical isolates from multiple human norovirus genotypes. Although several isolates replicated and could be serially passaged, replication was typically modest. Furthermore, multiple approaches commonly used to enhance viral replication in cell culture had little or no effect on system efficiency. These findings establish realistic expectations for the use of this model and provide a framework for future optimization of human norovirus cultivation systems.

abstract_zh: 摘要 诺如病毒(HuNoVs)是全球范围内非细菌性急性胃肠炎的主要病因。HuNoVs在培养方面极具挑战性,目前的细胞培养系统,如人肠类器官,在效率和可扩展性方面存在局限,这限制了其在食品安全研究中的应用。最近的研究表明,转化的唾液腺细胞系(包括NS-SV-TT-DC)能够支持诺如病毒 GII.4病毒的复制和传代。在此,我们探讨是否可以在唾液腺细胞中独立观察病毒复制,并检查其他人类诺如病毒毒株是否能在这些细胞中复制。为此,我们首先通过感染包被病毒囊或粪便滤液中的总病毒,评估了多种诺如病毒毒株在NS-SV-TT-DC细胞中的复制情况。观察到病毒复制水平较低,且病毒囊的分离并未提高复制效率。随后,我们筛选了来自9种基因型的50个诺如病毒样本,其中14个分离株显示出超过两倍的病毒复制。我们发现样本中的初始病毒载量对复制效率没有显著影响。我们还成功地传代了多个分离株。接着,我们检验了诸如Ruxolitinib、TPCA-1和BX795等干扰素抑制剂是否能提高病毒复制,但观察到效果微乎其微。最后,我们测试了多种补充剂,包括MgCl 2、胆盐、神经酰胺和TAK-779。大多数补充剂对HuNoV在NS-SV-TT-DC细胞中的复制几乎没有影响。胆盐和TAK-779显示出有限的、基因型特异性的益处。综上所述,这些结果表明唾液腺细胞仅能有限地支持某些HuNoV分离株的复制。重要性 缺乏强大且易于获得的细胞培养系统仍然阻碍了人类诺如病毒的研究。由于唾液腺细胞系易于维持且相对成本较低,它们最近成为人肠类器官的有希望替代品。在此,我们使用来自多种人类诺如病毒基因型的50个临床分离株,对NS-SV-TT-DC唾液腺模型进行了大规模独立评估。尽管某些分离株能够复制并进行连续传代,但复制通常较为有限。此外,多种常用于增强细胞培养中病毒复制的方法对系统效率几乎没有影响。这些发现为该模型的使用设定了现实的期望,并为未来优化人类诺如病毒培养系统提供了框架。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估人类诺如病毒(HuNoVs)在唾液腺细胞中的复制,以解决当前HuNoVs细胞培养系统的局限性,这些系统在培养病毒方面存在困难,从而限制了食品安全研究的进展。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究使用转化的唾液腺细胞系(NS-SV-TT-DC)来评估来自9个基因型的50个诺如病毒样本的复制情况,未提及具体的人类或动物受试者。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员通过感染NS-SV-TT-DC细胞,使用包被囊泡的病毒或粪便滤液中的完整病毒来评估病毒复制;筛选了50个诺如病毒样本的复制情况,并测试了多种补充剂和抑制剂以增强复制。
analysis_zh.main_results: 观察到病毒复制水平较低,且囊泡分离并未提高复制效率。在50个样本中,有14个分离株显示出超过两倍的病毒复制,初始病毒载量对复制效率没有显著影响。某些补充剂和抑制剂显示出有限的、基因型特异性的益处。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究提供了NS-SV-TT-DC模型的大规模评估,表明尽管某些分离株能够复制并进行传代,但复制通常较为有限,且常见的增强复制方法对系统效率几乎没有影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为该模型的使用设定了现实的期望,并为未来优化人类诺如病毒培养系统提供了框架,这可能有助于食品安全研究和相关研究。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括观察到的有限复制以及常见增强复制方法缺乏显著效果,这限制了对模型效用的信心。证据强度为中等。

title: Gut microbiome-enteric virus interactions: mechanisms, clinical implications, and translational directions.
abstract: The gut microbiome influences epithelial barrier integrity, metabolite availability, mucosal immune tone, and vaccine responsiveness, all of which are relevant to enterically transmitted viral infection. Norovirus and rotavirus primarily replicate in the intestinal mucosa and cause acute gastroenteritis, whereas poliovirus replicates in the gut and may disseminate systemically. Hepatitis A virus and hepatitis E virus are acquired through the intestine and shed fecally, but their dominant clinical manifestation is hepatitis. This review synthesizes evidence linking the bacteriome, phageome/virome, and mycobiome with these viruses, while explicitly distinguishing direct enteric virus mechanisms from broader microbiome-immune or metabolite pathways and from cross-kingdom evidence extrapolated from intestinal inflammation or pathobiont studies. The strongest evidence supports selected virus-bacterium and virus-metabolite mechanisms, including bacterial glycan interactions in norovirus, bacterial LPS-mediated poliovirus stabilization, bile acid-dependent human norovirus replication in enteroids, and rotavirus-associated barrier disruption. Human studies remain dominated by stool-based associations that are difficult to separate from inflammation, diet, antibiotic exposure, diarrhea, and sampling time. We therefore rank evidence across experimental, organoid, animal, human observational, and clinical-translational levels, and highlight concrete applications for severe gastroenteritis risk prediction, prolonged shedding, impaired barrier recovery, and oral vaccine nonresponse. Future progress will require longitudinal, spatially resolved, multi-kingdom, and multi-omics studies linked to human-relevant experimental systems.

abstract_zh: 肠道微生物组影响上皮屏障完整性、代谢物可用性、粘膜免疫张力和 疫苗 反应性,所有这些都与肠道传播的病毒感染相关。诺如病毒 和轮状病毒主要在肠粘膜中复制并引起 急性胃肠炎,而脊髓灰质炎病毒在肠道中复制并可能全身传播。甲型肝炎病毒和戊型肝炎病毒通过肠道获得并经粪便排出,但其主要临床表现是肝炎。这篇综述综合了细菌组、噬菌体/病毒组和真菌组与这些病毒之间的联系,同时明确区分了直接肠道病毒机制与更广泛的微生物组免疫或代谢途径以及从肠道炎症或致病生物研究中推断出的跨界证据。最有力的证据支持选定的病毒-细菌和病毒-代谢机制,包括 诺如病毒 中的细菌聚糖相互作用、细菌 LPS 介导的脊髓灰质炎病毒稳定性、肠类中胆​​汁酸依赖性人类 诺如病毒 复制以及轮状病毒相关的屏障破坏。人类研究仍然以基于粪便的关联为主,这些关联很难与炎症、饮食、抗生素暴露、腹泻和采样时间分开。因此,我们对实验、类器官、动物、人类观察和临床转化水平的证据进行了排序,并强调了在严重胃肠炎风险预测、长期脱落、屏障恢复受损和口服 疫苗 无反应方面的具体应用。未来的进展将需要与人类相关的实验系统相关的纵向、空间解析、多领域和多组学研究。

title: A Platform Approach to mRNA Purification by Tangential Flow Filtration: Application to a Pentavalent Norovirus Vaccine
abstract: Background/Objectives: Multivalent mRNA vaccines are being evaluated for prevention of norovirus infection caused by multiple circulating strains. Platform purification processes may accelerate development and reduce manufacturing complexity by enabling multiple mRNA constructs to be processed using a common downstream workflow. This study aimed to develop a high-yielding tangential flow filtration (TFF) process for a pentavalent norovirus vaccine comprising five VP1-encoding mRNA constructs from genotypes GI.1, GII.2, GII.3, GII.4 and GII.6. Methods: TFF studies evaluated membrane MWCOs, transmembrane pressures, shear rates, mRNA loadings, and scale-up. Process performance was assessed based on mRNA recovery, integrity, functionality, and apparent hydrodynamic size. Results: Although the VP1 constructs had similar molecular weights (590–610 kDa), initial studies using 100 kDa membranes revealed construct-dependent losses due to permeation of full-length mRNA. Apparent hydrodynamic size was associated with observed membrane sieving behavior, suggesting that transcript-specific structural properties may influence membrane transmission. Reducing the membrane MWCO from 100 to 50 kDa eliminated detectable mRNA permeation while maintaining membrane performance. A shear rate of 4000 s−1 supported higher mRNA loading without compromising recovery or integrity. The resulting 50 kDa process was successfully scaled from 40 cm2 to 1600 cm2 and achieved product yields exceeding 95% across all five VP1 mRNA constructs. Conclusions: These findings support a framework for developing standardized TFF conditions for multivalent mRNA vaccines. The results indicate that transcript molecular weight and nominal membrane MWCO alone may not predict mRNA retention and demonstrate the applicability of a common TFF process across five VP1 mRNA constructs. The proposed influence of RNA conformation on membrane transmission requires confirmation using orthogonal structural methods.

title: Comparable Norovirus Shedding in Symptomatic and Asymptomatic Individuals: A Hospital-Based Study in Bangladesh
abstract: Abstract Background The frequent detection of norovirus in the stool of healthy people may be due to prolonged norovirus shedding after recovery from illness or asymptomatic infections. We describe norovirus shedding patterns in symptomatic and asymptomatic persons in Bangladesh. Methods We enrolled acute gastroenteritis (AGE) cases and non-AGE controls from two hospitals from January–September, 2023. Fecal samples were tested for norovirus by rapid antigen testing and confirmed by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Positive persons were retested at days 20, 40, 60, and 120 by RT-qPCR. Shedding duration was calculated as the number of days from enrollment to the midpoint between the last norovirus-positive and first norovirus-negative specimens. Cycle threshold (Ct)-values served as an inverse proxy for the viral load. Results Among 16 persons confirmed infected with norovirus (11/32 AGE cases; 5/28 non-AGE controls), a total of 74 stool samples were collected from enrollment through follow-up, of which 28 (38%) were norovirus positive. Of these, 20 (71%) were typed as GII.4 Sydney[P16], 1 as GII.3[P16], and 7 as GII untypeable. The median duration of norovirus shedding was similar between AGE cases (10 days, interquartile range [IQR]: 9.5–29 days) and non-AGE controls (9.5 days, IQR: 9.5–49 days). Norovirus Ct-values varied substantially between persons and overlapped significantly among AGE cases and non-AGE controls. Conclusions The quantity and duration of norovirus shedding was similar between AGE cases and asymptomatic controls, complicating the attribution of norovirus infection to AGE in Bangladesh. Larger longitudinal studies would more accurately characterize norovirus shedding in resource-limited settings.

title_zh: 有症状和无症状个体的 诺如病毒 脱落情况相当:孟加拉国的一项医院研究
source_body_en: Abstract Background The frequent detection of norovirus in the stool of healthy people may be due to prolonged norovirus shedding after recovery from illness or asymptomatic infections. We describe norovirus shedding patterns in symptomatic and asymptomatic persons in Bangladesh. Methods We enrolled acute gastroenteritis (AGE) cases and non-AGE controls from two hospitals from January–September, 2023. Fecal samples were tested for norovirus by rapid antigen testing and confirmed by real-time quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR). Positive persons were retested at days 20, 40, 60, and 120 by RT-qPCR. Shedding duration was calculated as the number of days from enrollment to the midpoint between the last norovirus-positive and first norovirus-negative specimens. Cycle threshold (Ct)-values served as an inverse proxy for the viral load. Results Among 16 persons confirmed infected with norovirus (11/32 AGE cases; 5/28 non-AGE controls), a total of 74 stool samples were collected from enrollment through follow-up, of which 28 (38%) were norovirus positive. Of these, 20 (71%) were typed as GII.4 Sydney[P16], 1 as GII.3[P16], and 7 as GII untypeable. The median duration of norovirus shedding was similar between AGE cases (10 days, interquartile range [IQR]: 9.5–29 days) and non-AGE controls (9.5 days, IQR: 9.5–49 days). Norovirus Ct-values varied substantially between persons and overlapped significantly among AGE cases and non-AGE controls. Conclusions The quantity and duration of norovirus shedding was similar between AGE cases and asymptomatic controls, complicating the attribution of norovirus infection to AGE in Bangladesh. Larger longitudinal studies would more accurately characterize norovirus shedding in resource-limited settings.

title: Isothermal cross-priming amplification for field-deployable norovirus surveillance: a cost-effective and rapid solution
abstract: ABSTRACT Norovirus remains a leading cause of foodborne gastroenteritis globally. While isothermal amplification technologies offer advantages over traditional reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) in terms of speed and portability, there is a lack of domestically developed isothermal amplification systems for norovirus in China. Using a domestic patented cross-priming amplification (CPA) technology, we established CPA systems targeting the predominant norovirus genotypes GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17. The systems were evaluated using 224 fecal samples with confirmed genotypes via sequencing. Our lab-developed CPA (Lab-CPA) systems demonstrated high sensitivity, detecting 98.0% (49/50) of GII.3, 100% (80/80) of GII.4, and 96.9% (31/32) of GII.17 samples, with 100% specificity across all genotypes. Compared to certified clinical RT-qPCR kits, the total percent agreement was 98.7%, 99.3%, and 96.9% for GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17, respectively, accompanied by a significant linear correlation in threshold times. Crucially, the Lab-CPA systems reduced processing time by 44–60 min compared to RT-qPCR. Successful integration into the commercial EasyNAT platform using all-in-one cartridges further streamlined the workflow while maintaining accuracy. Our CPA systems offer a rapid, cost-effective, and streamlined diagnostic solution, ideally suited for point-of-care testing in resource-limited primary healthcare environments. IMPORTANCE Norovirus remains a critical public health threat, driving demand for rapid, deployable diagnostics. While isothermal amplification offers theoretical advantages over reverse transcription quantitative PCR, the absence of domestically developed systems in China has created a reliance on imported assays, limiting point-of-care testing capabilities. This study addresses that gap by establishing a novel cross-priming amplification system tailored to China’s predominant norovirus genotypes. Achieving high sensitivity/specificity and significantly reducing processing time, this work validates a robust, field-adaptable alternative to conventional methods. Furthermore, successful integration with the commercial EasyNAT platform demonstrates immediate translational potential. By providing a cost-effective, high-performance domestic solution, these findings significantly enhance decentralized surveillance and emergency response capacity for norovirus infections in resource-limited settings.

Using a domestic patented cross-priming amplification (CPA) technology, we established CPA systems targeting the predominant norovirus genotypes GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17. The systems were evaluated using 224 fecal samples with confirmed genotypes via sequencing. Our lab-developed CPA (Lab-CPA) systems demonstrated high sensitivity, detecting 98.0% (49/50) of GII.3, 100% (80/80) of GII.4, and 96.9% (31/32) of GII.17 samples, with 100% specificity across all genotypes. Compared to certified clinical RT-qPCR kits, the total percent agreement was 98.7%, 99.3%, and 96.9% for GII.3, GII.4, and GII.17, respectively, accompanied by a significant linear correlation in threshold times. Crucially, the Lab-CPA systems reduced processing time by 44–60 min compared to RT-qPCR. Successful integration into the commercial EasyNAT platform using all-in-one cartridges further streamlined the workflow while maintaining accuracy. Our CPA systems offer a rapid, cost-effective, and streamlined diagnostic solution, ideally suited for point-of-care testing in resource-limited primary healthcare environments. IMPORTANCE Norovirus remains a critical public health threat, driving demand for rapid, deployable diagnostics. While isothermal amplification offers theoretical advantages over reverse transcription quantitative PCR, the absence of domestically developed systems in China has created a reliance on imported assays, limiting point-of-care testing capabilities. This study addresses that gap by establishing a novel cross-priming amplification system tailored to China’s predominant norovirus genotypes. Achieving high sensitivity/specificity and significantly reducing processing time, this work validates a robust, field-adaptable alternative to conventional methods. Furthermore, successful integration with the commercial EasyNAT platform demonstrates immediate translational potential. By providing a cost-effective, high-performance domestic solution, these findings significantly enhance decentralized surveillance and emergency response capacity for norovirus infections in resource-limited settings.

title: A-305 Prevalence of Co-Detection with Ecoli-subtypes in Multiplex Gastrointestinal Panels
abstract: Abstract Background Syndromic gastrointestinal multiplex PCR panels have transformed enteric pathogen diagnostics by enabling rapid detection of multiple organisms, including Escherichia coli pathotypes. However, the clinical significance of these detections, particularly in pediatric populations, remains uncertain. Commonly used, 22-target multiplex panels frequently identify subtypes such as enteropathogenic (EPEC), enteroaggregative (EAEC), and enterotoxigenic (ETEC), often alongside other pathogens. This co-detection complicates interpretation and may influence inappropriate antibiotic prescribing, especially when the pathogenic role of E. We aimed to characterize the most frequent co-detections with EPEC, EAEC, and ETEC. Methods We analyzed electronic health record data from the Truveta EHR platform for patients tested with multiplex GI panels in acute care settings (emergency departments and inpatient units). Panels were identified using a comprehensive algorithm which leveraged specific CPT and LOINC codes. We assessed the top five pathogens which were co-detected with EAEC, EPEC, and ETEC pathogens. Co-detection was defined as =2 pathogens on a single panel. Prevalence was calculated as the proportion of patients positive for both pathogens among those tested for both. Codetection proportions were compared using binomial confidence intervals calculated with the Wilson score method. Treatment rates with antibiotics (Azithromycin (macrolide), Ceftriaxone (3rd gen cephalosporin) and Ciprofloxacin (fluoroquinolone) were assessed for EPEC, EAEC and ETEC groups and co-detected pathogens. Results The total number of panels identified was 9472, of which 38.9% were positive for any pathogen within the panel. Overall prevalence of EPEC, and ETEC were 7.9% (7.4-8.5), 3.8% (3.4-4.3) and 1.9% (1.7-2.2) among pathogens that were reported across the panels. Among samples positive for Escherichia coli pathotypes, co-detection with other enteric pathogens was frequent. The most common co-detections for:Among EPEC cases (N=728), the most frequently co-detected pathogens were norovirus (13.8%), followed by EAEC (13.0%), ETEC (7.7%), Campylobacter spp. (7.4%), and Clostridioides difficile (6.5%).Among EAEC cases (N=267), common codetections included EPEC (35.6%), ETEC (18.0%), Shigella/EIEC (13.1%), norovirus (11.6%), and Campylobacter spp. (9.7%).Among ETEC cases (N=178), codetections most frequently involved EPEC (31.4%), EAEC (26.9%), norovirus (15.1%), Clostridioides difficile (9.5%), and Campylobacter spp. Across all subsets, viral (Norovirus) and bacterial pathogens (Shigella, Campylobacter) were identified alongside E. coli pathotypes underscoring the complexity of interpreting multiplex PCR results in clinical practice. Viral codetections were common among E. coli–positive specimens, led by norovirus (13.6%) with 49% receiving E. coli–directed treatment, alongside similarly high antibiotic use with rotavirus A (32%), astrovirus (31%) and adenovirus 40/41 (30%). These patterns suggest that EAEC and EPEC, often asymptomatic colonizers may contribute to unnecessary antibiotics when co-detected with viral pathogens, underscoring the need for diagnostic stewardship and careful interpretation rather than reflexive treatment based solely on multiplex panel results. Conclusion Frequent co-detection of E. coli pathotypes with other enteric pathogens complicates clinical interpretation and may contribute to inappropriate antibiotic use. These findings highlight the need for enhanced diagnostic stewardship, including clinician education on interpreting multiplex results. analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,大肠杆菌致病型与其他肠道病原体的频繁共同检测使临床解释变得复杂,并可能导致抗生素的不当使用。这些发现强调需要加强诊断管理,包括对临床医生解释多重结果的教育。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,诊断管理和仔细解释多重检测结果对于避免不必要的抗生素使用是必要的,特别是当病毒病原体与大肠杆菌同时检测时。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对电子健康记录数据的依赖而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差或信息缺失。证据是中等的,因为它基于仅抽象的分析。

title: Measuring enteric pathogen force of infection through antibody responses in children
abstract: Enteric pathogens account for a substantial global disease burden, yet population-based surveillance remains limited by the transient nature of pathogen shedding, which constrains the sensitivity of stool-based molecular testing to a narrow detection window. Detection of IgG responses in serological surveys could enable new insights into enteric pathogen transmission, but benchmarking serological measures relative to stool-based measures of infection remains a critical evidence gap. We compared measures of disease transmission in longitudinal birth cohort samples using multiplex IgG (1,601 dried blood spots, 370 children) and PCR assays (2,231 stool samples, 370 children) that overlapped for nine pathogens (norovirus GI, GII, Shigella/enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC), Campylobacter spp., enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (LT-ETEC), Salmonella enterica, Giardia spp., Cryptosporidium spp., Entamoeba histolytica). LT-ETEC and Campylobacter ranked highest while E. enterica ranked lowest by both IgG and PCR measures of infection. Measures of infection were less aligned for norovirus GI, norovirus GII, Cryptosporidium, Shigella/EIEC, and Giardia. Despite this, for most pathogens, and across both measures, force of infection was lowest in the urban city of Esmeraldas and substantially higher in more rural populations, with relative risks in assay measures (seroconversion rate and PCR detected prevalence) over 2.0 for pathogens with the largest differences (Shigella/EIEC and norovirus GI). Together, our results suggest that although absolute levels of infection differed between assays, IgG and PCR captured consistent relative risk of infection across geographic strata, suggesting either method can identify high- versus low-transmission settings.

title_original: Measuring enteric pathogen force of infection through antibody responses in children

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human noroviruses, specifically Norovirus GI and GII, and their role in causing gastroenteritis in children. The central question is how to measure the force of infection of these viruses using antibody responses in serological surveys, with a comparison to stool-based molecular testing.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of longitudinal birth cohort studies that compared IgG antibody responses in dried blood spots (1,601 samples, 370 children) with PCR assays on stool samples (2,231 samples, 370 children) for nine enteric pathogens, including Norovirus GI and GII. The study design involved overlapping samples across pathogens, and the methods included serological and molecular testing.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that IgG and PCR assays captured consistent relative risk of infection across geographic strata, suggesting either method can identify high- versus low-transmission settings. For most pathogens, including Norovirus GI and GII, the force of infection was lowest in urban areas and higher in more rural populations.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is heterogeneity in the alignment of infection measures for certain pathogens, including norovirus GI, norovirus GII, Cryptosporidium, Shigella/EIEC, and Giardia. Additionally, benchmarking serological measures against stool-based measures remains a critical evidence gap.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review highlights the need for further research to benchmark serological measures against stool-based molecular testing for enteric pathogens. It also suggests that serological surveys could provide valuable insights into norovirus transmission dynamics, particularly in rural populations where the force of infection is higher.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the use of serological and molecular methods to measure the force of infection of human noroviruses, specifically GI and GII, in children. It compares IgG antibody responses in dried blood spots with PCR results from stool samples across nine pathogens, including norovirus. The study finds that both methods capture consistent relative risk patterns across geographic strata, with higher infection rates in rural areas. However, there is heterogeneity in the alignment of infection measures for some pathogens, and benchmarking serological data against stool-based testing remains a critical gap. The findings suggest that serological surveys could be useful for identifying high- versus low-transmission settings, particularly for norovirus GI and GII. The review emphasizes the need for further research to validate these methods and improve understanding of norovirus epidemiology.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注人类 诺如病毒,特别是 诺如病毒 GI 和 GII,以及它们在引起儿童胃肠炎中的作用。核心问题是如何使用血清学调查中的抗体反应来测量这些病毒的感染力,并与基于粪便的分子检测进行比较。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对纵向出生 队列研究 研究的系统分析,该研究将干血斑(1,601 个样本,370 名儿童)中的 IgG 抗体反应与粪便样本(2,231 个样本,370 名儿童)的 PCR 检测结果进行比较,以检测九种肠道病原体,包括 诺如病毒 GI 和 GII。研究设计涉及病原体的重叠样本,方法包括血清学和分子检测。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,IgG 和 PCR 检测捕获了跨地理层一致的感染相对风险,这表明任何一种方法都可以识别高 传播 环境与低 传播 环境。对于大多数病原体,包括 诺如病毒 GI 和 GII,城市地区的感染力最低,而农村人口的感染力则更高。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 某些病原体的感染措施存在异质性,包括 诺如病毒 GI、诺如病毒 GII、隐孢子虫、志贺氏菌/EIEC 和贾第鞭毛虫。此外,将血清学测量与基于粪便的测量进行基准测试仍然是一个关键的证据差距。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要进一步研究,以针对肠道病原体粪便分子检测来确定血清学措施的基准。它还表明,血清学调查可以为 诺如病毒 传播 动态提供有价值的见解,特别是在感染力较高的农村人口中。

We compared measures of disease transmission in longitudinal birth cohort samples using multiplex IgG (1,601 dried blood spots, 370 children) and PCR assays (2,231 stool samples, 370 children) that overlapped for nine pathogens (norovirus GI, GII, Shigella/enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC), Campylobacter spp., enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (LT-ETEC), Salmonella enterica, Giardia spp., Cryptosporidium spp., Entamoeba histolytica). LT-ETEC and Campylobacter ranked highest while E. enterica ranked lowest by both IgG and PCR measures of infection. Measures of infection were less aligned for norovirus GI, norovirus GII, Cryptosporidium, Shigella/EIEC, and Giardia. Despite this, for most pathogens, and across both measures, force of infection was lowest in the urban city of Esmeraldas and substantially higher in more rural populations, with relative risks in assay measures (seroconversion rate and PCR detected prevalence) over 2.0 for pathogens with the largest differences (Shigella/EIEC and norovirus GI). Together, our results suggest that although absolute levels of infection differed between assays, IgG and PCR captured consistent relative risk of infection across geographic strata, suggesting either method can identify high- versus low-transmission settings.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注人类 诺如病毒,特别是 诺如病毒 GI 和 GII,以及它们在引起儿童胃肠炎中的作用。核心问题是如何使用血清学调查中的抗体反应来测量这些病毒的感染力,并与基于粪便的分子检测进行比较。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对纵向出生 队列研究 研究的系统分析,该研究将干血斑(1,601 个样本,370 名儿童)中的 IgG 抗体反应与粪便样本(2,231 个样本,370 名儿童)的 PCR 检测结果进行比较,以检测九种肠道病原体,包括 诺如病毒 GI 和 GII。研究设计涉及病原体的重叠样本,方法包括血清学和分子检测。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该综述得出的结论是,IgG 和 PCR 检测捕获了跨地理层一致的感染相对风险,这表明任何一种方法都可以识别高 传播 环境与低 传播 环境。对于大多数病原体,包括 诺如病毒 GI 和 GII,城市地区的感染力最低,而农村人口的感染力则更高。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 某些病原体的感染措施存在异质性,包括 诺如病毒 GI、诺如病毒 GII、隐孢子虫、志贺氏菌/EIEC 和贾第鞭毛虫。此外,将血清学测量与基于粪便的测量进行基准测试仍然是一个关键的证据差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调需要进一步研究,以针对肠道病原体粪便分子检测来确定血清学措施的基准。它还表明,血清学调查可以为 诺如病毒 传播 动态提供有价值的见解,特别是在感染力较高的农村人口中。

title: Aircraft wastewater virome surveillance from domestic and international flights reveals viral diversity among travellers: A proof-of-concept study from Gujarat, India.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aircraft wastewater surveillance (AWS) at airports is an emerging method for detecting pathogens shed by international and domestic travellers. Global spread of infectious diseases occurs rapidly through air travel, and implementing surveillance systems at airports can help identify emerging viruses and track pathogens at scale. We aimed to characterize the viral diversity shed by travellers, which may represent routine viral circulation or active infection, at Ahmedabad airport in Gujarat. METHODS: We collected wastewater samples from domestic and international terminals where domestic flights connect to 18 states and 3 Union Territories, while international flights operate across 16 destinations in 11 countries. Samples were collected from June 2024 to November 2025. We used a capture probe-based enrichment approach for virome surveillance and detected multiple viruses of public health importance. RESULTS: We identified a total of 40 viral families and 315 viral species, with a median of 71 genomes/segments detected per sample in domestic wastewater and 48.5 genomes/segments per sample in international wastewater. We detected several respiratory and enteric viruses, including Influenza A virus, SARS-CoV-2, Human mastadenovirus A, Human mastadenovirus B, Noroviruses, Rotavirus A, Hepatitis A virus, Astrovirus MLB1, Human mastadenovirus F. Among these, certain viruses showed relatively higher mean RPKMF abundance in either domestic or international wastewater samples such as Bovine rotavirus A, Human rotavirus ID45/2, and BK polyomavirus observed in international wastewater samples, whereas Aichivirus A1, Norovirus GII.2, and Human immunodeficiency virus 1 showed higher abundance in domestic wastewater samples. We also detected multiple Influenza virus subtypes, including Influenza A subtypes H1N1, H3N2, H5N1, H7N1, and H9N2, along with Influenza B and Influenza C viruses. CONCLUSIONS: Continuous surveillance can provide early warning signals to public health authorities, timely decision-making and coordinated responses can reduce the spread of disease which also requires collaboration with national and international health authorities.
journal: Infection, genetics and evolution : journal of molecular epidemiology and evolutionary genetics in infectious diseases

title: Epidemiological Characteristics and Changes in the Trends of Other Infectious Diarrhoeal Diseases in Zhoushan, China, from 2016 to 2025
abstract: Abstract Background This study aims to investigate the epidemiological characteristics and changes in the trends of other infectious diarrhoeal diseases in Zhoushan from 2016 to 2025 to provide evidence for the optimization of disease prevention and control strategies. Methods The population distributions of cases of other infectious diarrhoeal diseases were acquired from the China National Infectious Disease Network Direct Reporting System (CNIDNDRS). A descriptive epidemiological framework was applied to characterize incidence, seasonality, and demographic distribution, while ‌Joinpoint regression analysis‌ was employed to detect significant inflection points in the secular trend, adjusting for the 2020 pandemic interference. Results: A total of 15,493 cases of other infectious diarrhoeal diseases were reported during the study period, with an average annual incidence rate of 132.78 per 100,000 population. No fatal cases were reported. Seasonal peaks occurred in winter (December–February) and summer (July–September). The male-to-female sex ratio was 1.24:1. The highest number of cases occurred in the 0ཞ4-year-old group (10,584 cases, 68.31%), predominantly among children living in household settings (9,282 cases, 59.91%). Aetiological agents were identified in 25.99% of the reported cases. Viruses and bacteria accounted for 96.35% and 3.65% of the confirmed pathogens, respectively. Rotavirus was the leading viral pathogen (3,067 cases, 79.05%), while Salmonella was the predominant bacterial pathogen (130 cases, 88.44%). A total of 23 clustered outbreaks were reported, mostly caused by norovirus (20 outbreaks, 86.96%), with all the clusters occurring in schools or childcare facilities. Joinpoint regression analysis revealed a three-phase trend in the overall incidence: an increase from 2016 to 2018 (APC = 17.54%, P = 0.01), followed by a decrease from 2018 to 2023 (APC=-12.50%, P Conclusions According to the results of Joinpoint regression, other infectious diarrhea cases in Zhoushan,China, exhibit obvious seasonal characteristics, and show an upward trend. To better prevent and control the situation, it is necessary that prevention and control efforts should prioritize outbreaks in schools and childcare settings, promote rotavirus vaccination, and increase laboratory diagnostic capacity in local medical institutions. The results established a critical evidence base for tailored enteric disease control in island and coastal populations globally.

title: Quantitative assessment of high-pressure processing inactivation of foodborne bacteria and viruses in foods
abstract: High-pressure processing (HPP) is a non-thermal food processing technology that can inactivate microbiological hazards while preserving product quality. This study compiled 2692 D -values across 15 microbial hazards pressurized at different pressures at a temperature ≤ 45 °C. The Bigelow model was used to estimate D ref values at P ref of 500 MPa. Based on these values, microbial hazards were grouped into three HPP resistance categories across all food matrices: 1) Sensitive ( D 500MPa ≤ 1 min): Vibrio spp., Aeromonas caviae , Campylobacter spp., Rotavirus, Cronobacter spp., Hepatitis A, Norovirus; 2) Moderate (1 3 min): Staphylococcus aureus , Bacillus cereus (vegetative cells) . However, food matrix composition strongly influenced microbial resistance to HPP: low water activity (a w ≤ 0.95) conferred protection, while acidic (pH ≤4.5) or high a w matrices (a w > 0.95) enhanced inactivation. Multiple linear regression identified microbial species, a w, and pH as significant predictors of the inactivation; other product characteristics, such as protein and carbohydrate content, showed limited effects. A decision-support framework was developed to evaluate microbial hazard resistance to HPP processing. abstract_zh: 高压加工 (HPP) 是一种非热食品加工技术,可以灭活微生物危害,同时保持产品质量。这项研究编制了 15 种微生物危害的 2692 个 D 值,这些危害在不同压力和温度 ≤ 45 °C 的条件下加压。Bigelow 模型用于估计 P ref 为 500 MPa 时的 D ref 值。根据这些值,所有食品基质中的微生物危害被分为三个 HPP 抗性类别: 1) 敏感(D 500MPa ≤ 1 分钟):弧菌属、豚鼠气单胞菌、弯曲杆菌属、轮状病毒、克罗诺杆菌属、甲型肝炎、诺如病毒;2) 中度(1-3分钟):金黄色葡萄球菌、蜡样芽孢杆菌(营养细胞)。然而,食品基质成分强烈影响微生物对 HPP 的抵抗力:低水分活度 (a w ≤ 0.95) 提供保护,而酸性 (pH ≤ 4.5) 或高 a w 基质 (a w > 0.95) 增强灭活作用。多元线性回归将微生物种类、w 和 pH 确定为失活的重要预测因子;其他产品特性,例如蛋白质和碳水化合物含量,显示出有限的影响。开发了一个决策支持框架来评估 HPP 加工的微生物危害抵抗力。该框架整合了三种互补方法:1) 500 MPa 下的微生物抗危害性排名,2) 按食品类别进行矩阵分层灭活估计,3) 使用 w 和 pH 作为自变量的多元线性回归模型。这些方法相辅相成,支持不同数据可用性场景下的微生物抗危害性评估。

title: Adsorption sequence shapes antigen distribution and antibody binding on adjuvants in bivalent vaccines
abstract: As a critical advancement in modern immunization strategies, multivalent vaccines combine multiple antigenic components to seamlessly broaden protection against diverse pathogens within a single dose. During the formulation of aluminum-adjuvanted vaccines, antigen adsorption onto the adjuvant surface serves as a critical determinant of vaccine performance. However, it remains unclear how the sequence of adsorption during formulation influences the particle-to-particle antigen loading heterogeneity on adjuvant particles and whether such differences are associated with immune outcomes. In this study, we systematically investigate how the adsorption sequence modulates particle-to-particle antigen-loading heterogeneity and antibody binding in bivalent vaccines. Using human papillomavirus (HPV16/18) and norovirus (NoV GI.1/GII.4) virus-like particles (VLPs) as model antigens with different adsorption strengths for amorphous aluminum hydroxyphosphate sulfate (AAHS), we demonstrate that the strength of antigen–adjuvant interaction is associated with how adsorption sequence influences antigen distribution. Antigens with weaker binding affinity exhibit distinct particle-to-particle antigen loading heterogeneity depending on the formulation sequence, whereas those with strong interactions remain largely unaffected. Importantly, these variations in particle-to-particle antigen-loading heterogeneity were associated with differences in antibody and monoclonal antibody binding, and with differences in in vivo humoral immune responses. These findings highlight adsorption sequence as an important formulation parameter associated with antigen distribution and antibody responses in multivalent vaccines.

However, it remains unclear how the sequence of adsorption during formulation influences the particle-to-particle antigen loading heterogeneity on adjuvant particles and whether such differences are associated with immune outcomes. In this study, we systematically investigate how the adsorption sequence modulates particle-to-particle antigen-loading heterogeneity and antibody binding in bivalent vaccines. Using human papillomavirus (HPV16/18) and norovirus (NoV GI.1/GII.4) virus-like particles (VLPs) as model antigens with different adsorption strengths for amorphous aluminum hydroxyphosphate sulfate (AAHS), we demonstrate that the strength of antigen–adjuvant interaction is associated with how adsorption sequence influences antigen distribution. Antigens with weaker binding affinity exhibit distinct particle-to-particle antigen loading heterogeneity depending on the formulation sequence, whereas those with strong interactions remain largely unaffected. Importantly, these variations in particle-to-particle antigen-loading heterogeneity were associated with differences in antibody and monoclonal antibody binding, and with differences in in vivo humoral immune responses. These findings highlight adsorption sequence as an important formulation parameter associated with antigen distribution and antibody responses in multivalent vaccines.

elements_zh.main_results: 研究发现,结合亲和力较弱的抗原根据配方序列表现出明显的颗粒间抗原负载异质性,而那些具有强相互作用的抗原基本上不受影响。这些变化与抗体和单克隆抗体结合以及体内体液 免疫应答 的差异有关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,吸附序列是影响多价 疫苗 中抗原分布和 免疫应答 的关键配方参数,突出了对 疫苗 设计因素的新理解。

abstract_zh: 作为现代免疫策略的关键进步,多价 疫苗 结合了多种抗原成分,可在单剂量内无缝地扩大对多种病原体的保护。在铝佐剂 疫苗 的配制过程中,佐剂表面上的抗原吸附是 疫苗 性能的关键决定因素。然而,目前尚不清楚配制过程中的吸附顺序如何影响佐剂颗粒上颗粒间抗原负载的异质性以及这种差异是否与免疫结果相关。在本研究中,我们系统地研究了吸附序列如何调节二价 疫苗 中颗粒间抗原负载异质性和抗体结合。使用人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV16/18) 和 诺如病毒 (NoV GI.1/GII.4) 病毒样颗粒 (VLP) 作为模型抗原,对无定形羟基磷酸硫酸铝 (AAHS) 具有不同的吸附强度,我们证明抗原-佐剂相互作用的强度与吸附序列如何影响抗原分布有关。结合亲和力较弱的抗原根据制剂序列表现出明显的颗粒间抗原负载异质性,而那些具有强相互作用的抗原基本上不受影响。重要的是,颗粒间抗原负载异质性的这些变化与抗体和单克隆抗体结合的差异以及体内体液 免疫应答 的差异相关。这些发现强调吸附序列是与多价 疫苗 中抗原分布和抗体反应相关的重要制剂参数。

title: Ionic-liquid-enhanced filtration membranes for simultaneous capture and inactivation of wastewater-relevant viruses and bacteria
abstract: Wastewater treatment is critical for mitigating global water scarcity, yet cost-effective, sustainable virus removal from municipal and hospital effluents remains challenging. Low-pressure polymeric membranes are attractive but usually lack virus selectivity. Here we developed carbon fiber–supported electrospun poly(vinylidene fluoride- co -hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) membranes incorporating tuneable, environmentally stable ionic liquids (ILs) to enhance virus adsorption and inactivation. Electrospun PVDF-HFP mats were modified with a hydrophobic IL comprising a pyrrolidinium-based cation and imide-based anion selected for fluoropolymer compatibility and known virucidal activity. Hybrid filters with microfiltration-range pores were challenged with influenza A virus (IAV) and murine norovirus (MNV) representing wastewater transported viruses. Low IL loadings (0.5–2 wt%) refined fiber and pore morphology and tuned surface charge and roughness while retaining hydrophobicity, enhancing capture via combined sieving and interfacial interactions. IL-modified membranes achieved up to a 5-log reduction value (LRV) for IAV, exceeding pristine membranes and benchmark targets of ≥4 LRV. The membranes also exhibited ≥80% porosity, bacterial rejection in crossflow filtration of up to 3 LRV and maintained permeate fluxes of ∼500 L m −2 h −1 (LMH) at ∼0.5 bar, supporting low-pressure operation. These results highlight IL functionalization of electrospun PVDF-HFP as a practical platform for improved virus removal in sustainable wastewater treatment.

Adhil Basha1, P. Balaganesan1*, R. Sengothai1, J. Renuka2 1Department of Mathematics, Academy of Maritime Education and Training (AMET) University, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India 2Department of Mathematics, Women’s Christian College, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India *Corresponding author. Balaganesan) ABSTRACT Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide, and its outbreaks in schools are sustained by person-to-person contact and by virus shed into the shared environment. We formulate a seven-compartment SEAIHRS–W model with asymptomatic infection, hospitalisation, waning immunity and an environmental reservoir. We prove positivity, boundedness and existence of a unique endemic equilibrium when R! > 1, derive R! by the next-generation matrix, and establish global stability of the disease-free equilibrium for R! < 1 and of the endemic equilibrium in the lifelong-immunity limit by Lyapunov functions. The system is solved by the multistage homotopy analysis method (MHAM), whose convergence on each stage is proven by a Banach fixed- point argument, with an explicit analyticity radius of at least 0.441 days. Calibrated to the 2001 Derbyshire primary- school outbreak (492 pupils, 201 cases), the model gives R! = 6.21 and an initial effective reproduction number of 3.99, with R" = 0.990 for cumulative cases. Against an RK45 benchmark over 60 days, the third-order MHAM attains a maximum relative error of 1.47 × 10#$% . Sensitivity analysis ranks environmental transmission, virus decay and shedding as dominant, supporting combined hygiene and cleaning interventions. Keywords: Norovirus, Environmental transmission, Multistage homotopy analysis method, Basic reproduction number, Lyapunov stability. Int J Drug Deliv Technol. 2026;16(85s): 1047- 1068; DOI: 10.25258/ijddt.16.85s.110 Source of support: Nil Conflict of interest: None 1. Introduction 1.1. Epidemiology and public health burden Norovirus causes an estimated one in five cases of acute gastroenteritis globally and is responsible for a large share of gastroenteritis-related hospitalisations and deaths, particularly among young children and older adults [1]. Global estimates cited in recent modelling work put the annual toll at about 685 million infections, including roughly 200 million in children under five, around 200,000 deaths and an economic burden near 60 billion US dollars from health-care costs and lost productivity [2]. In the United States alone, norovirus produces roughly 19– 21 million illnesses, 56,000–71,000 hospitalisations and 570–800 deaths each year [3]. Most deaths occur in older adults, while the largest number of medically attended cases occurs in young children [1, 3]. The disease is short and usually self-limiting. After a median incubation period of about 1.2 days [4], infected people develop vomiting, diarrhoea, nausea and abdominal cramps that usually resolve within a few days. Treatment is supportive, based on rehydration, and no licensed vaccine or specific antiviral is available [5]. Noroviruses are genetically diverse: they are classified into several genogroups, of which GI, GII and GIV infect humans, and genogroup II accounts for most human infections [5]. This diversity, together with immunity that wanes over several years [6], allows repeated infection throughout life and complicates vaccine design. An SEAIHRS–W Norovirus Transmission Model with Asymptomatic Shedding, Hospitalisation, Waning Immunity and An Environmental Reservoir: Analysis Via The Multistage Homotopy Analysis Method IJDDT, Volume 16 Issue 85s, 2026 Page 1048 1.2. Transmission routes and outbreak settings Norovirus spreads by the faecal–oral route through direct person-to-person contact, contaminated food and water, and contaminated surfaces. Very few virus particles are needed to cause infection, infected people can shed virus in faeces for weeks, and the virus can remain infectious on surfaces for up to about two weeks [5]. A substantial fraction of infections is asymptomatic. Asymptomatic carriers are less infectious than symptomatic cases, but they shed virus for longer and may therefore sustain transmission between visible outbreaks [7, 6]. These features make semi-closed settings especially vulnerable. Analysis of 7094 outbreaks reported to the US National Outbreak Reporting System during 2009–2017 found a median basic reproduction number of 2.75. Long-term care facilities had the highest setting-specific value, 3.35, and schools, colleges and universities had 2.92 [8]. Transmission was lowest in summer and peaked in autumn and winter [8]. In schools, projectile vomiting in classrooms contaminates shared spaces and exposes many children at once. Bayesian analysis of a 2001 primary-school outbreak in Derbyshire, England, showed that vomiting events were an important route of spread in addition to ordinary person-to-person contact [9]. The same outbreak is used in the present study to calibrate the model. 1.3. Mathematical models of norovirus Mathematical models have been used to estimate transmissibility, the duration of immunity and the effect of control measures. A review by Gaythorpe et al. [7] found published estimates of R! ranging from 1.1 to 7.2. Population-level estimates were generally close to 2, while estimates from individual outbreaks were higher and more variable. The review also noted that most population-level models use SEIR-type structures without explicit environmental compartments, and that asymptomatic infection and waning immunity deserved more attention. Simmons et al. [6] fitted a transmission model with asymptomatic infection to surveillance data from England and Wales and estimated that immunity lasts 4.1–8.7 years. This is far longer than the months suggested by early challenge studies. The environmental route has been examined explicitly in a smaller number of studies. Towers et al. [10] fitted a model with direct and environmental transmission to daily incidence from a cruise-ship outbreak. They estimated a combined reproduction number of 1.6 and found that direct transmission between passengers predominated in that setting. Wang et al. [11] fitted a model with two transmission routes to 23 school outbreaks in Jiangsu Province, China. They estimated mean effective reproduction numbers of 8.92 for person-to-person spread and 2.19 for water- or food-borne spread, and showed that isolating symptomatic cases sharply reduces peak incidence. A second line of work has focused on mathematical structure and numerical schemes. Raezah et al. [12] formulated a fractional-order model with vaccination and asymptomatic carriers under the Atangana– Baleanu–Caputo operator and solved it with an Adams–Bashforth scheme based on Newton polynomials. Cui et al. [13] combined a fractal– fractional operator with stochastic perturbations in a model with vaccination. Song et al. [14] studied a stochastic model driven by Lévy noise in which water and food contamination are explicit compartments. Ahmad et al. [15] analysed a fractional model with transmission through contaminated food and water. Saleem et al. [2] analysed a fractional SEIR model with a Grünwald– Letnikov nonstandard finite-difference scheme. Alqudah et al. [16] studied a discrete fractional SEAIRF model with an environmental reservoir and used a neural network to predict its dynamics. Several recent studies have combined analysis with control. Ndendya et al. [17] modelled vaccination, treatment and public-health education, computed the reproduction number by a graph-theoretic method and estimated parameters from US outbreak surveillance data for 2023–2024. Gogovi et al. [5] included environmental reservoirs, waning immunity and reinfection, proved global stability by Lyapunov functions and solved an optimal control problem. They found that the environmental transmission and shedding rates dominate the reproduction number and that hand hygiene is the most effective single intervention. 1.4. Semi-analytical solution methods Most of the studies above rely on numerical schemes, which give accurate trajectories but no explicit expression for the solution. Semi-analytical series methods instead produce closed-form approximations that show how each parameter enters the local dynamics and that can be differentiated directly. The homotopy analysis method (HAM) of Liao [18] constructs a continuous deformation from an initial guess to the exact solution. It contains an auxiliary convergence-control parameter ħ that can be used to enlarge the region of convergence. With a suitable choice of ħ, HAM reduces to the homotopy perturbation method and to the Adomian decomposition method. Sufficient conditions for convergence of HAM series were given by Odibat An SEAIHRS–W Norovirus Transmission Model with Asymptomatic Shedding, Hospitalisation, Waning Immunity and An Environmental Reservoir: Analysis Via The Multistage Homotopy Analysis Method IJDDT, Volume 16 Issue 85s, 2026 Page 1049 [19]. The Laplace–Adomian decomposition method has been applied to several epidemic models, including Lassa fever and malaria [20, 21]. A known weakness of all single-interval series methods is that a truncated series is accurate only near its expansion point. Epidemic curves evolve over weeks, so a single series is usually inadequate over the whole outbreak. The multistage homotopy analysis method (MHAM) restarts the series on short successive intervals and so extends the solution over long horizons. Its practical value, however, depends on knowing how long each interval may be before the series stops converging. Existing applications usually choose the step length by trial and error and verify convergence only numerically. 1.5. Research gap and contributions To our knowledge, no published norovirus model combines (i) asymptomatic infection with reduced infectiousness, (ii) hospitalisation with disease- induced death, (iii) waning immunity and (iv) an environmental reservoir, together with a semi- analytical solution whose convergence is proven rather than assumed. In addition, few norovirus models that include an environmental compartment have been calibrated to case data from a documented outbreak. This paper addresses these gaps. Its main contributions are as follows. 1. We formulate a seven-compartment SEAIHRS–W model and prove positivity, boundedness and existence of a positively invariant region. 2. We derive R! by the next-generation matrix and decompose it into direct and environmental contributions from asymptomatic and symptomatic carriers. We also obtain the endemic equilibrium explicitly. 3. We prove global stability of the disease-free equilibrium for R! < 1 by a Lyapunov function. For the endemic equilibrium we prove global stability only in the lifelong- immunity limit (ω= 0), by a Volterra-type Lyapunov function; with waning immunity (ω> 0) we establish local stability for the calibrated parameters. 4. We derive explicit MHAM solutions from zeroth to third order for every compartment. We prove convergence on each stage by a Banach fixed-point argument that yields a computable bound on the stage length. 5. We calibrate the model to the Derbyshire 2001 school outbreak, quantify uncertainty by parametric bootstrap, examine identifiability of the transmission routes and of the assumed environmental decay, test out-of-sample prediction, and validate the MHAM solution against an RK45 benchmark. 6. We quantify the sensitivity of R! , of the peak size and timing and of cumulative cases by Latin hypercube sampling with partial rank correlation, and evaluate combined hygiene and cleaning interventions. 1.6. Organisation of the paper Section 2 presents the model and its assumptions. Section 3 establishes the basic properties, equilibria and reproduction number, and Section 4 analyses local and global stability. Section 5 develops the MHAM solution and its convergence theory. Section 6 describes the data, calibration and numerical methods, and Section 7 reports the results. Sections 8–10 discuss the findings, limitations and public health significance, and Section 11 concludes. 2. The compartment W measures infectious virus in the shared environment, in normalised contamination units. The flow diagram is shown in Fig. 1.
